titulo: Präteritum: war, hatte and the modals: War and hatte

aula.titulo: Präteritum: war, hatte and the modals
aula.objetivo: Use the Präteritum of sein, haben and the modal verbs (konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte), choose between Präteritum and Perfekt in conversation, and recognize the most common Präteritum forms in texts.

blocos.texto: Lesson goal. By the end of the four sessions, you use war, hatte and the past-tense modals when you speak, form the Präteritum of regular verbs, recognize the most common irregular ones (ging, kam, sah, fuhr), and know when to use the Präteritum and when to use the Perfekt.

blocos.contexto: Jonas asks Camila why she looked so tired. Then, her diary.

linhas.ru: — Ja, sehr müde. Ich hatte viel Arbeit. Ich konnte nicht schlafen.
linhas.pt: — Yes, very. I had a lot of work. I couldn't sleep.
linhas.audio: Ja, sehr müde. Ich hatte viel Arbeit. Ich konnte nicht schlafen.

linhas.pt: — Did you have to work for a long time?

linhas.ru: — Ja, ich musste bis zehn Uhr arbeiten. Ich wollte früh gehen, aber ich durfte nicht.
linhas.pt: — Yes, I had to work until ten. I wanted to leave early, but I couldn't. Camila's diary. Yesterday was a long day. I woke up at six and took the bus to work. At the office I worked a lot. In the evening Jonas came over and we cooked together. Afterwards I watched a movie and fell asleep quickly.
linhas.audio: Ja, ich musste bis zehn Uhr arbeiten. Ich wollte früh gehen, aber ich durfte nicht.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: good news: the German Präteritum looks a lot like the English simple past — machte/made, kaufte/bought, kam/came, trank/drank. STEP 2: the trap is in usage: in everyday SPEECH, Germans use the Präteritum mainly for war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, durfte; for other verbs they say the Perfekt («Sie ist nach Hause gegangen»), and forms like «Sie ging nach Hause» belong mostly to stories and written texts. STEP 3: and "was + -ing" has no German equivalent: "I was working" is simply «Ich arbeitete» or, in speech, «Ich habe gearbeitet».

tabela.ingles: I had a lot of work.

blocos.titulo: Sein and haben in the Präteritum, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the «Präteritum» is the other past tense, used mostly in WRITING and in texts. STEP 2: with «sein» and «haben», CONVERSATION also uses the Präteritum instead of the Perfekt: you say «Ich war müde» (I was tired), not «Ich bin müde gewesen»; you say «Ich hatte Fieber» (I had a fever), not «Ich habe Fieber gehabt». STEP 3: the forms of «sein»: ich war, du warst, er war, wir waren, ihr wart, sie waren. STEP 4: the forms of «haben»: ich hatte, du hattest, er hatte, wir hatten, ihr hattet, sie hatten. STEP 5: notice that «ich» and «er» are IDENTICAL (war, hatte), just like the modals in the present tense.
blocos.comparacao: English is close here: "was" and "had" match «war» and «hatte» almost one to one — even the spelling: was/war, had/hatte. Just remember that German conjugates more: du warst, wir waren.

exemplos.ru: Ich hatte Fieber und war krank.
exemplos.pt: I had a fever and was sick.

exemplos.ru: Als Kind hatte ich einen Hund.
exemplos.pt: As a child I had a dog.

erros.errado: Du warst krank? — Ich waren krank.

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 sentences about yesterday and about your childhood with «war» and «hatte».
Write 6 Perfekt sentences, with «haben» and with «sein».
